model: Managed-care insurer normalised earnings (FCFE) capitalisation at cost of equity (engine route)

historical_growth.growth_rate_source: judgment: average of the base revenue path; FY2022-FY2025 annual figures for the CAGRs
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity (14.2% 5yr) and revenue (18.5% 5yr) CAGRs diverge by far more than 30% from EPS (-4.5% 5yr): revenue was bought through contract wins and acquisitions while margin collapsed in FY2025-26. Neither the equity nor the revenue CAGR is a usable forward rate; the base path is built from guidance and the OBBBA membership outlook instead.
historical_growth.notes: FCF CAGRs are not meaningful: reported FCF swings from +$2.0B (FY2021) to -$0.6B (FY2025) on the timing of government receipts and claims payments, and FY2025 is negative. SBC is small (0.1-0.3% of revenue) so the owner adjustment does not change the picture.

scenario_narratives.base: 2026 is the trough and 2027 state rate resets start the repair, but only partly. Total revenue is roughly flat in FY2027 (Marketplace and standalone MAPD each shed about $1B of premium, offset by Florida Kids, Illinois and Medicaid rate increases), then OBBBA work requirements and redeterminations hold growth to 3-4% through FY2029 before a 5-6% run driven by rates, duals and RFP wins. GAAP pretax margin recovers from ~0.4% in FY2026E to 1.4% in FY2027 (about $8.90 GAAP EPS, consistent with management's >$9.50 adjusted building blocks) and matures at 3.3% by FY2031 -- below the 3.7% FY2021-24 average because interest expense is higher, investment yields lower and the Medicaid risk pool sicker.
scenario_narratives.bull: Rates catch up with cost trend quickly: Medicaid MCR falls back toward 89-90% by FY2029, the Marketplace and MAPD exits prove to be a clean removal of loss-making premium, and the RFP win rate plus small-plan M&A put premium growth back at 8-9% in FY2029-31 (still short of management's 11-13% target). GAAP pretax margin reaches 4.3%, the level of FY2023, and the market pays 15x mature earnings.
scenario_narratives.bear: The rate-cost mismatch is structural, not cyclical: states under OBBBA provider-tax caps cannot fund adequate rates, Expansion membership falls 15-20% leaving a sicker pool, and one of the four big state contracts (CA, TX, WA, NY) is lost or repriced at re-procurement. Revenue shrinks through FY2028 and pretax margin never gets past 2.0% -- half the historical level -- with BB- leverage absorbing most of the parent's flexibility. A 10x exit multiple reflects a permanently lower-return franchise.

valuation_philosophy.summary: Molina is valued on the equity cash flow a capitated health insurer can actually distribute: net income on premium, less the statutory capital that growth locks in the regulated subsidiaries. The whole valuation is a judgment about where the pretax margin settles after the 2026 trough -- 2.0% (bear), 3.3% (base) or 4.3% (bull) against 3.2-4.3% in FY2021-24 and ~0.4% now. Terminal value is capped at an earnings-style multiple (10-15x) rather than left to Gordon growth.
key_risks_to_valuation: Margin level dominates: each 0.5pt of mature pretax margin is roughly 15% of base value, and FY2026 is running at ~0.4%.
Medicaid rate adequacy under OBBBA provider-tax caps and work requirements (phased 2027-2029); Expansion membership expected to fall 15-20%.
Contract concentration: CA, TX, WA and NY are more than half of Medicaid premium and are periodically re-procured.
Holding-company leverage: $3.77B of notes, BB-/Ba2, interest coverage covenant temporarily cut to 1.75x; the model assumes the debt is serviced and rolled, not repaid from the flows.
The -8% capital charge on revenue growth is an estimate from GAAP equity-to-revenue, not a disclosed risk-based-capital figure.
FY0 revenue is an estimate (9M actual plus guided Q4); the FY2026 10-K will replace it.

data_sources.price: Yahoo Finance chart API at inputs.price_as_of; 52-week range 121.06-244.89
data_sources.financials: MOH_Metrics.csv / MOH.duckdb (SEC XBRL); MOH_Quarterly_Q3-2026.txt for the balance sheet, share count, SBC, interest expense, investment income and parent-company cash; MOH_Annual_FY2025.txt
data_sources.qualitative: MOH_Analysis.json (guidance as of Q3 2026 earnings, 21-22 Oct 2026)

inputs.share_count_basis: 52.2M shares outstanding at 16 Oct 2026 (Q3-2026 10-Q cover) plus ~0.3M awards excluded from the diluted count as anti-dilutive; Q3 diluted weighted average was 51.5M. Held flat because SBC is expensed in the flows.
inputs.sbc_source: TTM to 30 Sep 2026 from cash flow statements: FY2025 $47M less 9M-2025 $27M plus 9M-2026 $85M (Q3-2026 10-Q line 1336). FY2025 was depressed by performance-award reversals; FY2024 was $116M. Shares withheld for employee taxes are immaterial (about 2,900 shares in Q3).
inputs.wacc_rationale: The discount rate is a COST OF EQUITY, not a WACC, because the flow is post-interest. USD basis: ~4.3% 10-year Treasury + 5.0% ERP x ~1.1 beta (thin-margin, single-payor, BB-/Ba2 holding company with 48% debt-to-capital) = ~9.8%, rounded to 10%. Same rate in every scenario; risk is charged once, through the scenario weights.
inputs.lease_treatment: Lease cost sits inside G&A and therefore inside the pretax margin; lease liabilities ($66M at FY2025) are not deducted again.
inputs.notes: MODEL: managed-care insurer, routed off the owner-FCF row. The skill's insurer row (BVPS compounding x exit P/B) fits balance-sheet compounders like Fairfax; Molina is a capitated, 1-4% margin underwriter whose value is earnings on premium, not book growth, so it follows this folder's financials convention instead: equity cash flow (FCFE) capitalised at the cost of equity with net_debt held at ZERO, run through the Drivers engine. Reported OCF/FCF is float noise (FY2025 -$636M, 9M-2026 +$535M on timing of state payments and claims) and is not the base. HOW THE ENGINE LINES MAP: 'EBITDA margin' = GAAP pretax margin on total revenue (after $215M/yr interest expense, including ~$400M/yr investment income on the float) + D&A + SBC; tax at 25.5%; D&A 0.35% vs capex 0.30% of revenue; 'working capital' at -8% of the revenue CHANGE is the statutory capital that premium growth traps in the regulated subsidiaries (equity is 9.4% of revenue, of which roughly 8% is required capital), and it releases when revenue shrinks. NOT DONE, DELIBERATELY: the $3,771M of senior notes is not deducted (its interest is already in the flow) and neither the $4.5B cash / $4.1B investments (they back $4B+ of medical claims payable and statutory capital) nor the $608M of parent-company cash is added -- the parent cash is left out as a cushion against a BB- balance sheet rather than treated as surplus. Investment income is NOT stripped, because the float that earns it is not added to value. FY0 is FY2026E (9M actual revenue $32,752M plus a guided Q4; premium revenue guidance ~$42B), not FY2025, because ten and a half months of 2026 are already earned and the first projected year should be the FY2027 recovery year. last_fcf/reported_fcf are TTM figures kept for the audit trail only; no projection compounds from them. Buybacks: nil in 9M-2026 after $1.0B in each of FY2024 and FY2025; $500M of authorisation remains but the flat share count is currently not being funded. Price is a regular-session close.

required_return_table.note: Each row rebuilds the terminal value at that row's rate (max(0, min(Gordon@r, 14x FCF_N))); the WACC row is valuation.base.intrinsic_value and the hurdle row is entry_price.base.entry_price.

sensitivity.note: Rows are WACC, columns terminal growth; each cell rebuilds its own terminal value.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Bear raised to 25% from the 15% default: earnings depend on a single class of payor (state Medicaid agencies and CMS), a 1-point MCR move is worth about $6 of EPS, the cost-trend assumption was still being raised in Q3 2026, and the parent is rated BB- with a temporarily loosened coverage covenant. Base 50%: management's own 2027 building blocks support a partial recovery without assuming any MCR improvement. Bull cut to 25% from 35%: it needs rate adequacy, a clean Marketplace/MAPD exit and a resumed RFP win streak to all happen while OBBBA is shrinking the pool.

sanity_check.basis: SBC-adjusted on both sides (EPS less SBC/share; EBITDA less SBC), so these deliberately do not match GAAP screener multiples.
